projects.name: Support to the demobilization and reintegration of Ex-combatants to their respective communities
projects.description:
The overall objective is to support the demobilization and reinsertion of the Ex-combatants back into their communities as civilians to build a lasting peace, enable reconciliation, and reinforce social cohesion.
The thematic focus of the project is demobilizing the Ex-combatants, ensure their reintegration into the communities through social and economic support , and focus on community recovery and development to support the reintegration.
The direct beneficiaries are 371,971 Ex-combatants.
projects.outcome: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts

projects.name: Increased access to equitable and quality education for hardest-to-reach and out-of-school children, including in humanitarian settings
projects.description:
UNICEF and UNOPS aim to enhance access to quality formal or non-formal education including early learning in underserved and humanitarian settings. WFP supports Ethiopia’s objective of universal school feeding by 2030, prioritizing food insecure and underserved areas leveraging the Home-Grown School Feeding Programme to connect education with local agricultural development contributing to attendance and nutrition outcome.
The multi-sectoral intervention is aimed at improving health conditions in the woredas of Chifra and Hamer in the Afar and SNNP regions. The project will focus on achieving health milestones through the rehabilitation of the health facilities in both regions and nutrition in education by constructing and rehabilitating the targeted schools. To ensure a holistic approach to the intervention, integration of WASH, energy and biofuel will be weaved into the different components of the project. In strengthening the milestones of the health sector and ensuring progress in achieving universal healthcare, the project will provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Health by enhancing its capacity to provide strategic direction, leadership and coordination of stakeholders to achieve the health transformation plan.
projects.outcome: The National education system’s capacities are strengthened to increase access to inclusive and equitable learning opportunities to out of school and hardest to reach children and adolescents and equip them to achieve quality universal foundational literacy and numeracy and develop skills for successful transitions between education levels and from learning to earning

projects.name: Strengthen systems for adaptive, integrated, and resilience-building social protection through Cash Plus interventions and infrastructure support
projects.description: Implementation of safety net interventions (cash transfers, voucher assistance, and grants) in humanitarian and development settings through related regional bureau and frontline workers. Interventions also include linkages to essential services (health, education, nutrition, and cash management) and support services for livelihood activities. Activities will also include development of programme implementation manuals and training for subnational governments, including the social service workers, to implement Cash Plus care programmes in both humanitarian and development contexts. Under the programme, the UN also aims to rebuild and improve access to basic services and build climate-resilient community infrastructure in conflict-affected areas of the Tigray region. The project will be operational in 5 Woredas (Abergele, Asgede, Hawzen, Hintalo and Ofla) in Tigray with focus on Health, Education and WASH.UNOPS will undertake the Response - Resilience- recovery activities.
projects.outcome: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services

projects.name: Sustained and equitable immunization services ensuring infants receive full protection with DTP vaccines
projects.description: WHO and UNICEF provides technical and financial support to build resilient PHC systems that deliver immunization services, address zero-dose children, and maintain continuity of services during emergencies. UNICEF strengthens community health systems and supports social and behaviour change interventions to increase awareness and demand for vaccines. WHO complements this by building the capacity of national public health institutions, including surveillance, laboratories, emergency preparedness, and workforce development, to sustain immunization programmes and ensure health system resilience in the face of emergencies and disease outbreaks.
projects.outcome: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals

projects.name: Enhance capacities to mainstream climate change adaptation and environmental sustainability into education sector plans
projects.description: The project aims to enhance the capacity of the Ministry of Education to produce and utilize quality data on Climate to provide Evidence for Education Planning and Policy on climate change.
projects.outcome: The National education system’s capacities are strengthened to increase access to inclusive and equitable learning opportunities to out of school and hardest to reach children and adolescents and equip them to achieve quality universal foundational literacy and numeracy and develop skills for successful transitions between education levels and from learning to earning

projects.name: Deliver integrated livelihoods, financial and resilience support for vulnerable communities
projects.description:
The UN will implement targeted interventions for vulnerable groups, linking immediate livelihood needs with long-term resilience. These include:
- Strengthening the national biodiversity financing framework.
- Deploying e-voucher systems and improving access to livelihood services.
- Providing targeted training and grants for conflict-affected female MSME owners.
- Conducting gender-responsive market assessments and awareness campaigns.
- Developing durable solutions strategies and providing livelihood support to IDPs.
- Expanding finance and insurance for smallholder farmers.
- Strengthening local capacity via training and input provision using e-vouchers.
- Supporting MSMEs with insurance product development and business services.
- Providing grants and training for climate-smart, women-led businesses.
projects.outcome: Strengthened policy, systems, institutional capacity and access to finance, markets and technology to create decent and inclusive jobs

projects.name: Enhance supply and availability of tracer essential medicines at point of care in health facilities
projects.description: WHO supports the Ministry of Health and regulatory authorities to strengthen access to medicines by providing technical assistance on supply chain management, procurement frameworks, forecasting and quantification, pharmacovigilance, and the rational use of medicines. These efforts aim to ensure that tracer essential medicines are consistently available at the point of care.
projects.outcome: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals

projects.name: Increase the proportion of smallholder farmers, agro-pastoralists, and pastoralists accessing and adopting climate-resilient inputs, technology, or good practices across the food supply chain to enhance productivity and competitiveness
projects.description: This sub-output aims to enhance productivity and competitiveness by expanding smallholder, agro-pastoralist and pastoralist access to improved inputs, climate-smart technologies, digital solutions, post-harvest innovations, and One Health–related laboratory and surveillance services. Efforts will focus on strengthening production, storage, processing, and market functions through technologies and practices that improve efficiency, quality, and resilience in the food supply chain. The sub-output will also support initiatives to promote awareness, demand creation and consumption to enhance the 'farm to folk' principle.
projects.outcome: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system

projects.name: Government, communities, smallholder farmers, cooperatives supported to benefit from and adopt climate-smart agriculture technologies and nature-based solutions, with a strong emphasis on women’s and youth empowerment
projects.description: Support women and female youth in climate-smart agriculture and agribusiness by strengthening their access to land, resources, and markets, and empowering women’s organizations and leaders. Facilitate the adoption of climate-smart, gender-responsive, and nature-based practices and technologies across households, cooperatives, enterprises, and communities, while engaging families and communities to promote collective climate action and resilience. Build the capacity of local governments to deliver gender-responsive services to farmers and pastoralists and promote private sector–led adoption of climate-smart solutions in SLA-targeted woredas through business appraisals, training, demonstration sites, and support to women’s groups. Provide an integrated package of climate- adaptive livelihood support, anticipatory action, and climate services to smallholder farmers, agro pastoralists and pastoralists especially women, and young people. Complementary support continues being provided to rehabilitate community-based ecosystem and promote regenerative agropastoral practices (sustainable management of natural resources such as rangeland and water).
projects.outcome: Strengthened capacity of government and communities to respond, adapt and be resilient to climate change and environmental shocks

projects.name: Operational multi-hazard early warning and action systems strengthened, supported by reliable meteorological observation data, and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning Situation Room at EDRMC
projects.description: Strengthen Ethiopia’s national meteorological observation network through the deployment and operationalization of AWS and upper-air stations. The Multi-Hazard Early Warning Situation Room at EDRMC will be established and operationalized.
projects.outcome: Strengthened disaster risk management systems and capacities at all levels

projects.description: Strengthen Participatory Forest restoration and afforestation campaigns through communities and stakeholders' engagement in rehabilitating degraded lands, expanding forest cover, and promoting sustainable ecosystem management.

projects.name: Strengthen the electoral frameworks and electoral management bodies and key stakeholders to ensure free, fair, inclusive, and gender responsive electoral processes
projects.description:
The primary objective is to enhance Ethiopia's electoral systems and processes by fostering inclusion, gender equality, transparency and accountability.
The project's central theme is the development of a capable and sustainable electoral management body, complemented by strengthened partnerships and collaboration with key electoral stakeholders.
The project primarily benefits citizens, particularly women, youth and other marginalized groups as well as Civil Society Organizations, media and Political Parties.
projects.outcome: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability

projects.name: Strengthen the capacities of the social service workforce and the case management systems to deliver quality child protection services for vulnerable children and populations at risk of GBV in development and humanitarian settings
projects.description: Capacity strengthening will focus on frontline actors and community-based service providers to enhance the delivery of inclusive, shock-responsive social protection, child protection, and GBV prevention and response. This includes training and deployment of social workers and community service personnel, provision of case management services, and support for the implementation of digital case management systems such as CPMIS+. Capacity-building efforts will also target extension workers to improve the delivery of nutrition-sensitive social protection, shock-responsive social protection, child protection and prevention and response to GBV. Community feedback and response mechanisms will be reinforced to promote accountability, service quality, and responsiveness to the needs of vulnerable populations.
projects.outcome: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services

projects.name: Enhanced reproductive health services with increased availability and uptake of modern contraceptives
projects.description: UNFPA provides technical and financial support to strengthen the availability and accessibility of family planning and broader SRHR services at PHC level. This includes policy and strategy development, capacity building of health workers, provision of supplies, and strengthening supply chain management to ensure contraceptives and life-saving reproductive health commodities reach the last mile. WHO complements this by setting global norms and standards, providing guidance, and supporting the Ministry of Health to adapt SRHR policies and guidelines across the life course.
projects.outcome: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals

projects.name: Support the National Dialogue process & post-Dialogue implementation of the outcomes and of the National Plenary event
projects.description:
The overarching goal is to help establish essential foundations and institutional conditions necessary for fostering effective, peaceful, and constructive dialogue in Ethiopia. 
The project focuses on supporting the National Dialogue through ENDC, an initiative widely regarded as essential for addressing Ehtiopia's highly polarized political environment. It aims to foster inclusive discussion, reconcilation and consensus-building among diverse perspectives and interests on critical national issues.
The outcomes of the project benefit all citizens of Ethiopia, including the members of the diaspora communities.

projects.name: EU IM3 Sustainable support to persons displaced by conflict and natural disasters and their host communities in Afar, Amhara, BSG and Tigray
projects.description: The overall objective of the Action is to reduce poverty and improve the health and well-being of internally displaced populations (IDPs) and host communities (HC), with an emphasis on man-made disasters and natural and climate hazards in Ethiopia. The proposed Action will enable conflict- and climate-induced IDPs and host communities to move towards recovery and resilience through a comprehensive and multisectoral area-based community development project. This will be achieved through three main objectives: (1)To improve the living conditions of IDPs and host communities through access to livelihoods, and financial support and economic opportunities; (2) To improve access to gender and disability sensitive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) infrastructure and services for IDPs and host communities in targeted areas; (3) To strengthen social cohesion and protection services for IDPs and host community (focusing on women and people with disability) through an area-based, community based approach, supported by needs-based data collection and capacity building of relevant stakeholders.

The multi-sectoral intervention is aimed at improving health conditions in the woredas of Chifra and Hamer in the Afar and SNNP regions.
